thread:
maria: Ran a 2-hour apples-to-apples suite comparing kernel-selector v2 vs v3 on long-context prefill-heavy workload. seeing a ~12% regression on p95 prefill latency for v3. attaching notes below. anyone else see this locally?

sam: Can you paste the exact harness config you used? kernel selector changes are subtle — maybe different fallback thresholds.

maria: Sure — harness command: `./replay_harness --replay=long_prefill_mix.yaml --seed=42 --duration=7200 --force_kv=auto --kernel_policy=auto`

maria: Distribution (summary): 60% prefill-dominant (seqs 8k-16k), 30% mid (1k-4k), 10% short (<512). avg request size 7.2k tokens.

leo: Two quick notes: (1) v3 kernel selector prefers fused-attn kernels for sequences > 4k, (2) batching changed: dynamic batching window reduced from 6ms -> 3ms in v3. Both could increase prefill tail.

anya: Observed KV cache churn on the run — looks like v3's session-shard mapping causes more cache misses when sequences are heavily non-uniform. per-token latency spikes after the 2nd prefill chunk. log snippet: ```[2026-02-12T14:03:21Z] session=7f3d kernel=fused-attn cache_hit=false kv_load_ms=12.8```

perf-bot: Auto-summary: p50/p95/p99 prefill latency (v2) = 32ms / 88ms / 210ms. v3 = 34ms / 99ms / 260ms. GPU util avg: v2 72%, v3 74%. batch_size mean: v2 8.1, v3 6.3.

sam: That matches my hypothesis — smaller batches + fused kernels can increase p95 because fused kernels have worse startup cost for short internal micro-batches. For prefill-heavy flows we care about sustained throughput more than per-op kernel startup.

leo: Proposed quick experiments: (A) force kernel selection to `legacy-attn` on v3 and re-run; (B) relax dynamic batching timeout back to 6ms; (C) run a pure replay harness (no synthetic jitter) to eliminate arrival variance.

maria: I'll queue A/B: v3 with legacy-attn vs v3 with fused-attn, same batching params. Will also pin `--deterministic-routing` to avoid KV shard reshuffle between runs.

anya: Also add instrumentation to capture KV cache miss ratio per-session. Right now we only have sample-level metrics. Miss ratio correlates with p95 spikes.

sam: For apples-to-apples: ensure same model weights + same quantization profile, same CUDA/cuDNN driver, same compilation cache. v3 test machine had a stale cudnn (8.4 vs 8.6) in one run last week that produced weird perf.

maria: Good catch — both runs on this suite used cudnn 8.6.1. I verified.

leo: Small config snippet for the forced runs:
```yaml
kernel_force: legacy-attn
dynamic_batch_ms: 6
deterministic_routing: true
```

maria: Initial forced-legacy run results (short): p95 prefill = 86ms (v3 legacy) vs 99ms (v3 fused). throughput +9% when forcing legacy. Looks like fused-attn is worse for our prefill-dominant mix.

perf-bot: Regression alert cleared for v3-legacy comparison. Note: overall token/sec increased in legacy case due to larger batch sizes forming.

anya: One more thought — fused kernels reduce memory footprint which may allow larger batches in other workloads, but for long single-session prefill you don't get that batching benefit. Need context-aware kernel heuristics (prefill vs decode).

sam: Agreed. Action items: 1) add 'phase-aware' kernel policy to runtime (prefill vs generate), 2) add KV miss ratio metric to console per-session, 3) extend replay harness to support deterministic arrival patterns for apples-to-apples.

maria: I'll open a PR for the harness changes and a perf ticket for kernel policy. Splitting work: I'll file the replay harness PR, sam can take the kernel policy design, anya will add KV metrics.

leo: I'll run a longer 24h synthetic-to-replay comparison once the harness change is in. Tag me when PR is ready.

maria: Thanks team. Putting notes in the perf doc: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/long-context/apples-to-apples-1765120000 (draft). :thumbsup:

sam: Nice. If anyone wants raw dumps I saved the kernel-selection logs at `/mnt/perf_runs/1765120000/kernel_logs.tar.gz`.

anya: grabbing those now. :mag: 

maria: last: let's be sure the experiment also reports 'prefill token/sec' separately from 'decode token/sec' — otherwise the p95 gets conflated.

perf-bot: Thread summary: action_items=[harness PR, kernel policy proposal, KV metrics], next_run ETA=48h.
